findings.what: The question says that whether sing(M) may be empty, or every α ∈ A must occur, is something « the paper does not say ». ETT is silent, but gx's def:atlas, which DEC-25 adopts, speaks to both halves (papers/gx/legacy/labeled/RamcovGX.tex:1905-1917). (a) « An X_A-chart is an X_α-chart for some α ∈ A », and an X_A-manifold only has to admit an X_A-atlas, so not every α ∈ A need occur. DEC-25 settles this half. (b) An X_α-chart is a chart around x ∈ sing(M), and an X_A-atlas is « a collection of X_A-charts covering M ». Read literally, this forces sing(M) ≠ ∅ for M ≠ ∅, and more: every point lies in a chart around a singular point. The library already weakens this to covering Sing(M) (SFALocal.MassACovered; Causal/GXSingularDEC25.lean checklist, « ⚠ weakened: only the singular points need an X_A-chart (gx's X_A-atlas covers M …) »). That is the Lean ≥ paper direction. Every theorem of this file holds in both readings, and the witnesses E₀ and E_π satisfy the literal one (identity charts around an axis or line point cover the model). The question blocks no statement and no mark. It is not genuinely open in a way that needs OQ-87.
findings.fix: Open no OQ. Record the reading in def:singular_spacetime's notes (curation text below). Optionally add one SCOPE sentence to the file: « sing_α(M) may be empty: gx's def:atlas read as covering Sing(M), as Causal.GXSingularDEC25 does; read literally (« covering M ») it forces sing(M) ≠ ∅, and every theorem here holds in either reading ».

question_review.question: Must a singular flat spacetime have a non-empty singular locus, or every α ∈ A occurring? (proposed OQ-87)
question_review.answer: Neither half needs a new OQ. 'Every α ∈ A occurring' is settled by DEC-25, which adopts gx's def:atlas: « an X_A-chart is an X_α-chart for some α ∈ A » (RamcovGX.tex:1910), and an X_A-manifold only admits an X_A-atlas. 'Non-empty singular locus': gx's « X_A-atlas … covering M » (l.1911), with X_α-charts around singular points (l.1908), read literally forces sing(M) ≠ ∅ for M ≠ ∅. The library has already taken, and disclosed, the weaker reading, which covers Sing(M) only (MassACovered; Causal/GXSingularDEC25.lean checklist, ⚠ weakened). The SingularFlat and SingularGeroch SCOPEs carry the consequence (« the sets sing α may be empty », timelikeLine_singularFlatAxioms). No DEC rules the literal-versus-weak cover, but no statement or mark depends on it. Every theorem here is stated for every E≥0-manifold, so it holds in both readings, and E₀ and E_π satisfy the literal one. The REPORT's « The paper does not say » should read « ETT does not say; gx's def:atlas, read literally, gives sing(M) ≠ ∅, and the library's MassACovered weakens it ». Record this in notes, not as an OQ row.

def:singular_spacetime.notes_append: T-ett-singular-sfa (atlas-team, 2026-11-21), audit AUDIT-1 minor (a duplicated generic lemma disclosed, findings routed to notes, the empty-locus question recorded as a reading; fixed at graduation), Causal/Port/SFAManifolds.lean: the definition implies the library's abstraction.
